$comment:
Part-content-encoding case table, shared byte-for-byte by the three engines that build an OpenAPI
form request body — openbindings-go/formats/openapi, openapi-client/go and
openapi-client/typescript/src — and by openbindings-ts/packages/openapi, which re-exports the
TypeScript engine and executes the same table against its BUILT dist. Each case is rendered as a
WHOLE OpenAPI document and loaded through the engine's own loader, so the table exercises the
shipped path rather than a hand-built typed model.

WHAT THIS TABLE GUARDS. `contentEncoding` changes a form part's default Content-Type in exactly one
row, and every accepted 3.1 edition scopes that row to `type: string`:

  3.1.0   §4.8.14.5  "If the property is a `type: string` with a `contentEncoding`, the default
                      Content-Type is `application/octet-stream`"
  3.1.1   §4.8.15.1.1 table: `string` x contentEncoding present -> application/octet-stream
  3.1.2   §4.8.15.1.1 table: the same row, and the same note

The 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 tables say the converse in their own words: "The default values for contentType
are as follows, where an n/a in the contentEncoding column means that the presence or value of
contentEncoding is irrelevant" — and n/a is what the `number, integer, or boolean`, `object` and
`array` rows hold. 3.1.0 reaches the same place because its only encoding-keyed bullet is the
`type: string` one and its primitive bullet carries no encoding condition. The incorporated dialect
agrees independently: JSON Schema 2020-12 §8.3 opens "If the instance value is a string, this
property defines that the string SHOULD be interpreted as encoded binary data", §8.4 opens "If the
instance is a string, this property indicates the media type of the contents of the string", and
§8.1 makes the whole Content vocabulary annotations that "do not function as validation
assertions".

So the table's claim, asserted separately from the cells:

  On the 3.1 line, with no Encoding Object, a part's decision is IDENTICAL with and without
  `contentEncoding` for every kind whose declared type is not `string` — and DIFFERENT for
  `string`, which is what makes the row real rather than vacuous.

THE 3.0 LINE IS A DIFFERENT CELL AND IS NOT FOLDED IN. `contentEncoding` is not in the 3.0 Schema
Object's dialect: counted against the pinned edition texts with corpus-lab/scripts/strip-oas-html.mjs,
`contentEncoding` occurs 0/0/0/0/3/11/18/19 times over 3.0.0, 3.0.1, 3.0.2, 3.0.3, 3.0.4, 3.1.0,
3.1.1, 3.1.2 — and none of 3.0.4's three occurrences is in its §4.7.15.1.1 default table, which keys
on `type` x `format`. The 3.0 editions' own encoding-keyed multipart bullet names a different
keyword entirely: "If the property is a `type: string` with `format: binary` or `format: base64`
(aka a file object), the default Content-Type is `application/octet-stream`", verbatim in 3.0.0,
3.0.1, 3.0.2 and 3.0.3. That `format` cell is open item F-O1-10 item 1 and this table does not touch
it; the 3.0 rows here exist to pin that both spellings of a kind decide identically under that line.

THE TYPELESS CELL IS NOT THIS TABLE'S TO DECIDE. OAS 3.1.1 and 3.1.2 give a part with `type` absent
the default `application/octet-stream`, for which `openbindings.openapi@1` defines no JSON-to-octet
part boundary, so a typeless part carrying `contentEncoding` refuses; 3.1.0 states no typeless row
at all. That conflict with §9.2's degenerate-combinations convention is filed as F-O1-10 item 2 and
is recorded here as observed, not resolved.

THE DECLARED-`encoding.contentType` COLUMN IS PINNED AS OBSERVED. Where an Encoding Object declares
`contentType`, no per-type default is consulted — every accepted edition defines the field as "The
Content-Type for encoding a specific property" — so what the part carries is the implementations'
shared carriage rule for that concrete media type. Those cells exist because they are where the two
engines actually diverged before 2026-08-17: both Go engines refused a part whose schema carried
`contentEncoding` and whose declared type was not `string` BEFORE reading the declaration at all,
while TypeScript honoured it. Measured over the six kinds x eight editions x two form media x three
`encoding.contentType` columns, that was 18 diverging cells, all on the 3.1 line and all in the
declared `text/plain` column.

THE URLENCODED LANE CARRIES TWO OPEN ITEMS OF ITS OWN, neither decided here: which serialization
path an edition selects (`legacyOpenAPIFormEncoding`, audited and closed as F-O1-10 item 3) and the
content lane deriving an array property's default from the ARRAY rather than its items (open item
20). Its rows are pinned as observed.
